question: Why is inheritance by lineage considered appropriate in traditional law?
premises: Traditional law texts prescribe inheritance through lineage.
This prescription is fitting because it reflects degrees of closeness.
The distinction between near and distant relations justifies graded inheritance.
inference: Inheritance rules in traditional law are grounded in the graded closeness of bodily lineage.
plain_english: And so, in the traditional law texts, inheritance by lineage is indeed fitting, since it is determined by the distinction between nearer and more distant relations.
